Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical opacity (indicated by the arrow) and absence of the right second rib, which are classic radiographic signs of a Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) with local invasion. In a 75-year-old smoker, this malignancy is the most likely diagnosis, and the disorientation episodes may be related to paraneoplastic syndromes or metastatic disease associated with lung cancer.
